Energetics, Incorporated (1998). Energy and Environmental Profile of the U.S. Petroleum Refining Industry. Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Industrial Technologies, Columbia, Maryland, December 1998. No report number or DOI printed.

Region: United States, base year 1996 (capacities 1 Jan 1997 at 93% utilisation). Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 3). Statistical profile: no capex, opex, CO2 per unit or whole-refinery configurations, so refinery_hydroskimming/conversion/deep-conversion get nothing. Loaded: per-bbl final energy for 15 refinery process units plus Claus sulfur recovery, from the chapter energy tables (licensor-utility averages, HP 1996 / Meyers 1997 / ANL 1981). Per unit: fuel = printed TOTAL minus printed electricity; electricity converted from gross 10^3 Btu (10,500 Btu/kWh) back to kWh. TRAPS: (1) all printed electricity and totals are GROSS (primary equivalent); totals and Table 2-2 ranges are in other-values only. (2) The fossil-fuel split by carrier is an assumed refinery-wide 1996 mix applied identically to every unit (footnote a), so only the fuel total is loaded; split quoted in notes. (3) "Other" fuel includes purchased steam. (4) HF alkylation: Table 6-2 total 254.8 vs Table 2-2 401 (Table 6-2 loaded). (5) Delayed coking "Other" total-industry 14.6 inconsistent with 2.4 x capacity (specific value used). (6) FCC fuel row excludes regenerator coke burn. (7) Hydrogen consumption/production and exported steam go to flows (Btu per bbl). Units per bbl of feed (per bbl crude for distillation); service-unit m3, archetypes are per t - density conversion needed. Heating-value basis not stated (U.S. EIA convention is HHV).
